label: Early-position (t=1,2) token-pair detector: input in {x,e,g,0,z,f,r,o,n,h} right after f/0/x/r/e
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at positions 1-2 (96.6% of mass at t=1,2; a small tail at t=3, almost none at the delimiter, never in the copy phase). Within those positions it depends jointly on the current and previous token: strongest when the current input is x or e and the previous token is f or 0 (top activations: 0 f [e], 0 f [x], f f [e]), and generally when the input is in {x,e,g,0,z,f,r,o,n,h} and the previous token is in {f,0,x,r,e}. Magnitude is largest at t=1-2 for these x/e pairs. It does not fire at t=0 or t>=4, and it does not fire on the same tokens later in the sequence. The rule is a fuzzy pair lookup, so the clean predicate misses some lower-activation pairs (e.g. y->x, j->z) and over-predicts some listed pairs at t=2.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: f, 0, r, x, e, z; least: b, u, q, l) and the current input token, by step (t=1: x, e, g, n; t=2: x, e, g, z; t=3: x, e, g, z); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=1, L=3 & t=3.
